body_md: Note that the lower bound provided by \eqref{eq:infinite speed of propagation in thm statement} vanishes in the limit as $T \to \infty$, thus leading to (potentially) degenerate diffusion at infinite times. This observation is compatible with the segregated (and hence non-smooth) stationary states that were numerically obtained in \cite{bbes model}; \textit{cf.~}Figures 4 and 5 therein.

title: Proof
body_md: Recall that \eqref{eq:u eq} conserves its initial mass, \textit{i.e.~}directly from \eqref{eq:for rho initial data} with $\varphi = 1$, we have $ \Vert 1- \rho \Vert_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^2)} = \int_{\mathbb{T}^2} u \, \mathrm{d}  x = \int_{\mathbb{T}^2} u_0 \, \mathrm{d}  x =  \Vert 1- \rho_0 \Vert_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^2)}$ a.e.~$t>0$. It therefore follows, using also Lemma \ref{prop:lower bound rho improved small times only}, that for a.e.~$t \in (0,1)$ it holds $\Vert 1- \rho_0 \Vert_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^2)}  =  \int_{\mathbb{T}^2} u(\frac{t}{2},x) \, \mathrm{d}  x \leq |\mathbb{T}|^2 \operatorname*{ess \, sup}\limits_{(\frac{1}{4}t,\frac{3}{4}t)\times\mathbb{T}^2} u \leq |\mathbb{T}|^2 e^{Ct^{-10}} \operatorname*{ess \, inf}\limits_{(\frac{5}{4}t,\frac{3}{2}t)\times\mathbb{T}^2} u$, and the result follows.
